comment: DOM-XSS-style flow heuristics (0.52.0). JsFlowAnalyzer pairs a dangerous SINK with an attacker-controllable SOURCE appearing within a proximity window in the same JS body, and emits ONE actionable finding ('source -> sink, try X') instead of two noisy inventory hits. Sinks with always=true (eval etc.) are inherently dangerous and reported even with no nearby source. Passive/static (regex proximity, not a real taint/AST analysis) -- the 'test' hint tells the analyst how to confirm by hand. Bounded regex (ReDoS).

sources.name: window.name
sources.inject: window.name set from an attacker page

sources.name: postMessage data
sources.inject: a postMessage sent from another origin (check for a missing origin check)

sinks.name: innerHTML/outerHTML
sinks.test: feed an HTML payload such as and see if it executes

sinks.name: document.write
sinks.test: feed or a

sinks.name: jQuery .html()
sinks.test: feed an HTML/script payload into the value passed to .html()

sinks.name: location assignment (redirect / javascript:)
sinks.test: feed a javascript: URI or an external URL (open redirect)

sinks.name: eval()
sinks.test: if the argument is attacker-controllable, inject a JS expression such as alert(1)

sinks.name: Function constructor
sinks.test: inject a JS function body such as return alert(1)

sinks.name: setTimeout/setInterval string
sinks.test: if the string argument is attacker-controllable, inject JS, e.g. alert(1)
